terms.meaning: marking an item so it stands out for the user
opening a closed section to show more detail

sections.name: File setup, EventType
sections.title: Imports and event kinds
sections.what: Brings in icons, card and badge parts, a class joining helper and a button. It also defines the six event kinds: report, medication, diagnosis, visit, surgery and reminder.
sections.why: The six kinds decide the icon and colors shown for each entry in the health history.

sections.name: TimelineEvent
sections.title: Shape of one timeline event
sections.what: Describes one history entry: id, kind, title, sub line, date, and optional description, status, attachments and pinned flag.
sections.why: Gives the card a fixed set of fields. Optional fields let entries show only what they have.
sections.watch_out: Attachments can be plain text or an object with a name and link, so code that reads attachments must handle both forms.

sections.name: eventConfig
sections.title: Colors and icons for event kinds
sections.what: Maps each event kind to an icon and colors, such as a scissors icon in red for surgery and a calendar in grey for reminders.
sections.why: Helps users scan the history by kind.

sections.name: TimelineEventCard (part 1)
sections.title: Collapsed event row and pin button
sections.what: Shows one event as a row with an icon, title, status badge, kind, sub line and date. A pin button appears only when the parent supplies a pin action. Clicking the row opens or closes the details.
sections.why: Gives a compact view of the history, with the option to pin important entries.
sections.watch_out: The pin button stops the click from also opening the row, so removing that stop would make pinning open the details by mistake.

sections.name: TimelineEventCard (part 2)
sections.title: Expanded area with description and pin toggle
sections.what: Shows the pin button and an open or closed arrow. The arrow is kept on the right of the row. This section also draws the description text when it is opened.
sections.why: Lets users read the full description of an entry without leaving the timeline.

sections.name: TimelineEventCard (part 3)
sections.title: Attachments and action buttons when expanded
sections.what: When opened, lists attachments as links that open in a new tab, or as plain buttons when there is no link. It also shows Edit Details and Share with Doctor buttons.
sections.why: Lets users open source files for an entry and prepares for editing and sharing. Reason for the link handling is not fully stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Edit Details and Share with Doctor have no click action, so they do nothing. Attachment links open a new tab without a check on the address, so bad data could send users to unexpected pages.

summary: A clickable row for one health history entry (report, medication, diagnosis, visit, surgery or reminder) that expands to show more detail.
purpose: Shows a patient's health history in date order, with details on demand and an optional pin.
why: Header says chronological health history entry. The reasons for expanding and pinning are not stated in the code.
how: Picks an icon and color from the event type. Shows the title, type, subtitle, date and an optional status badge. Clicking the row opens or closes an extra section. When a pin handler is passed, a pin button appears. Clicking it stops the row from toggling and reports the new pin value.
inputs: A timeline event with id, type, title, subtitle, date, and optional description, status, attachments and pinned flag. Also an optional pin handler from the parent.
outputs: Opens or closes the extra section. Calls the pin handler with the event id and the new pinned value.
risks: The visible part ends inside the expanded section, so how descriptions and attachments are shown is not confirmed. Unknown event types use the reminder style. The pin icon only changes when the parent updates the data.
debug: If the wrong icon appears, check the event type value. If pinning does nothing, check that a pin handler is passed and that it updates the pinned flag. If the row opens when pinning, check that the click stop is still in place.
